context.analysis:
## Overview
The system gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern cloud-based platform while the legacy system processes ongoing claims. It provides a hybrid architecture ensuring seamless incremental migration of claim types without service disruption.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Operations and Support Staff
- Finance and Accounting
- Modern Claims Platform (Azure West Europe)
- Legacy Mainframe System (On-Premises COBOL/DB2)
- Enterprise Identity Provider (Active Directory / Entra ID)

## Relationships
- Customers, Brokers, Adjusters, Operations, Finance -> Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL)
- Modern Claims Platform -> Enterprise Identity Provider via OpenID Connect (OIDC) for Single Sign-On (R-07)
- Modern Claims Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe System via Asynchronous Messaging / Enterprise Service Bus using encrypted TCP/MQ with mTLS
- Modern Claims Platform -> Finance/Accounting via SFTP / encrypted API feeds for financial reconciliation

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service / Azure Container Apps: Hosts the Modern Claims Platform to meet the <2s performance requirement (R-05)
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging to respect strict nightly batch windows (23:00-05:00)
- Azure API Gateway / Anti-Corruption Layer: Isolates the platform from schema drift given the constraint of at most one mainframe interface change per quarter
- Azure Key Vault: Manages secrets and automated certificate rotation for hybrid mTLS endpoints
- Azure Monitor / App Insights: Distributed tracing and tamper-proof audit logs to guarantee zero lost claims (R-04)

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture allows incremental migration of claim types one by one while keeping the COBOL/DB2 mainframe as the system of record. Fully managed Azure services offset the team's cloud inexperience while maintaining strict consistency and performance constraints.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a modern cloud platform that gradually replaces a legacy mainframe claims system through a hybrid architecture. Its core purpose is to enable incremental claim type migration while ensuring zero data loss and maintaining business continuity.]

## Key Elements
* Web Frontend
* API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
* Core Claims Service
* Data Sync Engine
* Azure SQL Database
* Enterprise Identity Provider
* Legacy Mainframe System

## Relationships
* Web Frontend -> API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF): HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL)
* API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Core Claims Service: HTTPS/TLS (gRPC/REST)
* Core Claims Service -> Azure SQL Database: TDS (Tabular Data Stream) with encryption
* Data Sync Engine <-> Legacy Mainframe System: Encrypted TCP/MQ with mTLS via Enterprise Service Bus
* Web Frontend -> Enterprise Identity Provider: OpenID Connect (OIDC)

## Technology Stack
* React/TypeScript on Azure Static Web Apps: Serves adjusters and customers with a responsive interface
* Azure Container Apps (Node.js/Go): Implements API Gateway/BFF for caching and async orchestration
* Azure Container Apps (Java/Spring Boot or .NET): Hosts Core Claims Service domain logic
* Azure Service Bus & Azure Functions: Powers Data Sync Engine for reliable messaging
* Azure SQL Database: Acts as cloud system of record with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture decouples modern web clients from legacy mainframe latency to meet strict performance targets. Managed cloud services reduce operational burden for a team with limited cloud experience while ensuring reliable data synchronization.]

Web Frontend.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform using a hybrid cloud architecture. Its core purpose is to incrementally migrate claim types to a cloud-native platform while ensuring continuous business operations.]

## Key Elements
* Web Frontend (React/TypeScript on Azure Static Web Apps)
* Auth Component (TypeScript / MSAL.js)
* Customer Portal UI (React)
* Adjuster Workspace UI (React)
* Migration Feature Flag Adapter (TypeScript)
* API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Azure Container Apps (Node.js/Go))
* Core Claims Service (Azure Container Apps (Java/Spring Boot or .NET))
* Data Sync Engine (Azure Service Bus & Azure Functions)
* Azure SQL Database (Azure SQL Database)
* Legacy Mainframe System (COBOL/DB2)
* Enterprise Identity Provider (Active Directory / Entra ID)

## Relationships
* Customers and Brokers -> Web Frontend [HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL)]
* Claims Adjusters -> Web Frontend [HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL)]
* Web Frontend -> API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) [HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL)]
* Web Frontend -> Enterprise Identity Provider [OpenID Connect (OIDC)]
* API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Core Claims Service [HTTPS/TLS (gRPC/REST)]
* Core Claims Service -> Azure SQL Database [TDS with encryption]
* Data Sync Engine -> Legacy Mainframe System [Encrypted TCP/MQ with mTLS via Enterprise Service Bus]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the React/TypeScript frontend with global CDN distribution.
* Azure Container Apps: Runs the BFF and Core Claims Services using Node.js/Go and Java/.NET for scalable microservices.
* Azure SQL Database: Provides cloud data storage with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE).
* Azure Service Bus & Azure Functions: Powers reliable messaging and asynchronous data synchronization.
* MSAL.js: Manages OIDC authentication and Single Sign-On session tokens.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes while delivering high-performance cloud UI experiences under strict latency targets. It guarantees incremental migration with rapid fallback capabilities and robust security controls.]

* Modern Claims Platform -> Enterprise Identity Provider: OpenID Connect (OIDC)

## Technology Stack

Core Claims Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a cloud-based Core Claims Service hosted in Azure Container Apps that modernizes an insurance claims platform while integrating with an on-premises mainframe. Its core purpose is to process migrated claim types securely, maintain strict data consistency, and support gradual platform migration.]

## Key Elements
- Claim Domain Controller [component]
- Claim Processing Engine [component]
- Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) [component]
- Outbox Event Publisher [component]
- Repository / Data Access Component [component]

## Relationships
- Claim Domain Controller -> Claim Processing Engine [In-process method calls]
- Claim Processing Engine -> Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer [In-process method calls]
- Claim Processing Engine -> Outbox Event Publisher [JDBC / Transactional Outbox]
- Claim Processing Engine -> Repository / Data Access Component [In-process method calls]
- Repository / Data Access Component -> Azure SQL Database [TDS with encryption]
- Outbox Event Publisher -> Data Sync Engine [AMQP / Azure Service Bus]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps [Hosts the Core Claims Service with managed identities and revision support]
- Java / Spring Boot or .NET [Implements the Core Claims Service domain logic and components]
- Spring Data JPA / Entity Framework [Encapsulates persistence logic in the Repository component]
- Azure SQL Database [Acts as the cloud system of record using Transparent Data Encryption]
- OpenTelemetry [Enables distributed tracing across the hybrid boundary]

## Rationale
[This architecture uses domain isolation and a Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer to allow rapid one-day fallback of claim types to the legacy system. The Transactional Outbox pattern guarantees data consistency without complex distributed transactions, fitting a team with limited cloud experience.]

Data Sync Engine.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform via a hybrid architecture, gradually replacing the legacy mainframe while ensuring continuous operations.]
[The Data Sync Engine uses Azure Functions and Azure Service Bus to reliably synchronize claims between the cloud and the on-premises mainframe.]

## Key Elements
- Data Sync Engine [container] (Azure Service Bus & Azure Functions)
- Sync Ingestion Function [component] (Azure Functions (.NET))
- Mainframe Adapter Component [component] (Azure Functions (.NET))
- Dead-Letter & Reconciliation Handler [component] (Azure Functions (.NET))
- Idempotency Store [component] (Azure SQL Database)
- Legacy Mainframe System [externalSystem] (COBOL/DB2)
- Operations and Support Staff [person]
- Azure Monitor / Application Insights [externalSystem]
- Azure Key Vault [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Sync Ingestion Function -> Idempotency Store (TDS (Tabular Data Stream) with encryption)
- Mainframe Adapter Component -> Legacy Mainframe System (Encrypted TCP/MQ with mTLS via Enterprise Service Bus)
- Dead-Letter & Reconciliation Handler -> Azure Monitor / Application Insights (HTTPS/TLS (REST))
- Mainframe Adapter Component -> Azure Key Vault (HTTPS/TLS (REST))

## Technology Stack
- Azure Functions (.NET): Chosen for serverless execution, minimizing infrastructure management for a team with limited cloud experience.
- Azure Service Bus: Provides reliable messaging, queuing, and dead-letter handling to prevent data loss (R-04).
- Azure SQL Database: Powers the Idempotency Store for deduplication and exactly-once processing.
- Azure Key Vault: Secures mTLS client certificates and encryption keys for compliance and security.
- Azure Monitor / Application Insights: Delivers native observability without custom UI maintenance overhead.

## Rationale
[The component architecture ensures strict data consistency (R-04) and rapid rollback capabilities (R-06) through idempotency, circuit breaking, and dead-letter handling.]
[Leveraging managed Azure serverless services reduces operational complexity and matches the team's existing cloud capability profile.]

Azure SQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
The system is the Modern Claims Platform, designed to gradually replace a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system via a hybrid architecture. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submissions and modern claims handling while maintaining data consistency and supporting incremental migration.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Operations and Support Staff
- Finance and Accounting
- Legacy Mainframe System (COBOL/DB2)
- Enterprise Identity Provider (Active Directory / Entra ID)
- Web Frontend (React/TypeScript on Azure Static Web Apps)
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Azure Container Apps (Node.js/Go))
- Core Claims Service (Azure Container Apps (Java/Spring Boot or .NET))
- Data Sync Engine (Azure Service Bus & Azure Functions)
- Azure SQL Database (Azure SQL Database with Azure SQL Ledger and Change Tracking)

## Relationships
- Customers and Brokers -> Web Frontend (HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL))
- Claims Adjusters -> Web Frontend (HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL))
- Operations and Support Staff -> Web Frontend (HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL))
- Finance and Accounting -> Web Frontend (SFTP / encrypted API feeds)
- Web Frontend -> API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (HTTPS/TLS (REST/GraphQL))
- Web Frontend -> Enterprise Identity Provider (OpenID Connect (OIDC))
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Core Claims Service (HTTPS/TLS (gRPC/REST))
- Core Claims Service -> Azure SQL Database (TDS with TLS 1.2+ via Private Endpoint)
- Data Sync Engine -> Legacy Mainframe System (Encrypted TCP/MQ with mTLS via Enterprise Service Bus)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps with React/TypeScript for responsive frontend delivery
- Azure Container Apps (Node.js/Go) for API Gateway/BFF routing and orchestration
- Azure Container Apps (Java/Spring Boot or .NET) for domain logic execution
- Azure SQL Database with Azure SQL Ledger and Change Tracking for reliable cloud persistence and tamper-evident auditing
- Azure Service Bus and Azure Functions for asynchronous hybrid messaging and data synchronization
- Microsoft Entra ID for Single Sign-On and database authentication via Managed Identities

## Rationale
This architecture uses a hybrid approach with Azure Container Apps and Azure SQL Database to deliver sub-second adjuster screen loads and isolated cloud persistence. It ensures zero data loss and rapid one-day rollback capabilities to the legacy mainframe, mitigating migration risks for teams with limited cloud experience.
